messages:
maya: Heads-up — we've got multiple reports of users losing the `project-admin` role after yesterday's RBAC refactor + the Okta SAML attribute normalization change. Repro steps I used below.

jordan: ugh. seeing similar tickets from customer-success. any quick rollback option? :grimacing:

maya: Repro: 1) User signs SSO 2) SAML assertion contains `Groups` attribute (capital G) 3) Our new mapping only matches `groups` (lowercase) after normalization change 4) JIT provisioner creates user but role assignment skips because mapping misses value.

samir: thanks. can you paste the raw assertion?

maya: pasting redacted assertion snippet:
```xml
<Attribute Name="Groups">
  <AttributeValue>redwood-project-admins</AttributeValue>
</Attribute>
<Attribute Name="email">
  <AttributeValue>user@acme.com</AttributeValue>
</Attribute>
```

maya: Our mapping config (new) is: 
```yaml
okta:saml:attributes:
  groups: \<% Attribute:Groups %\>
  email: \<% Attribute:email %\>
```

alex: so the mapping engine normalized attribute names to lowercase and then looked for `groups` only? that seems backwards — older configs tolerated either.

okta-bot: Audit event: role_assignment_failed user=user@acme.com reason=missing_attribute mapping_key=groups ts=1779903501

jordan: we pushed a tight mapping rule to reduce stray group injections, but this is causing regressions. i'd prefer a quick patch to accept both `Groups` and `groups`.

samir: agreed. quick mitigations: 1) patch mapping parser to be case-insensitive OR 2) add fallback to check original attribute names before normalization OR 3) rollback PR that enforced strict normalization. Which is least risky?

maya: rollback is fastest but loses other safety checks. case-insensitive match seems low-risk and small. i've got a patch ready locally: 
```diff
- attr_key = attr_key.lower()
+ attr_key_norm = attr_key.lower()
+ if attr_key_norm == 'groups':
+   match_any = [attr_key_norm, 'Groups']
+ else:
+   match_any = [attr_key_norm]
```

alex: small nit — better to normalize mapping keys and also check original assertion map. don't hardcode 'Groups'. use a generic case-insensitive lookup.

maya: yep good call, i'll switch to a case-insensitive dict lookup. i'll open a hotfix PR to eng-releases and tag @jordan @samir for review.

okta-bot: Audit event: config_change user=maya action=open_pr repo=infra-mapper pr=542 ts=1779903622

jordan: please also add an audit log entry for any users impacted (role_unassigned events) so support can follow up. we need a runbook for communicating to customers.

maya: adding to PR: I will emit role_assignment_failed and role_unassigned events with correlation id and include in audit-export. Also will add a one-line migration note for on-prem customers.

samir: after patch and deploy let's run a smoke test: create SAML assertion with mixed-case attribute names and ensure roles assigned. i'll volunteer to run e2e.

alex: :thumbsup: Also add a small E2E for JIT onboarding in CI to prevent regression.

maya: will do. timeline: hotfix PR in 15m, prod deploy after +30m review, smoke test +1h. If any blockers i'll rollback.

jordan: thanks — post results here. i'll start drafting a short customer note for affected accounts.

maya: posted PR link in thread, monitoring.

samir: received. will run smoke tests once deploy ready.

okta-bot: Audit event: deploy initiated user=maya env=prod deploy_id=deploy-2026-03-18-07 ts=1779903860

maya: closing loop — hotfix deployed, smoke passed, and we've added case-insensitive mapping + CI test. customer success notified for impacted users.

jordan: awesome, thanks team.
